title: heuchera glabella var. suksdorfii
intro: Heuchera glabella var. suksdorfii, commonly known as Alaskan coral bells, is a perennial plant species in the saxifrage family, native to the Pacific Northwest region of North America. It is valued for its ornamental properties, with maple-like leaves in shades of red and pink, and its ability to attract pollinators and other wildlife. The leaves of Heuchera glabella var. suksdorfii have been traditionally used in herbal medicine, offering potential health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, and have been used to treat various health issues. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic acids, which are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties.
